_comment: Pinned facts for azure-to-aws DESIGN pass 1 over the azure-iac-terraform corpus. Same selection rule as expected-iac-terraform.json: only facts where a plausible improvisation and the correct answer DIVERGE. Identity is the Terraform ADDRESS, resolved to an azure_id through the run's own inventory, so these expectations survive any change to azure_id reconstruction.
_not_asserted: clusters[], pattern_id, target_architecture (build step 4); the specialist-gate rows (the corpus contains no Managed Instance, elastic pool, Synapse workspace, Data Factory, or SQL Server VM image, so no gate fires and none can be verified here); right-sizing and any dollar figure (Estimate, with tolerances).

table_self_checks._why: The design is only as trustworthy as the table it claims to have read. These checks run on the table itself, so a design that cites a row cannot be trusted more than the row's existence.
table_self_checks._required_direct_rows_why: Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets and the three storage-service children are the load-bearing entries: canonicalization emits them as their own child-typed resources, so removing a row does not merely lose a mapping — the type reaches the unknown-type policy, matches 'sits in a network/data provider namespace', and STOPS the design on every real estate.
table_self_checks._must_not_be_direct_rows_why: All compute, and any database whose target depends on the availability answer, must stay on the rubric path. Promoting one to Direct Mappings would stamp `deterministic` on a target a pattern or a Clarify answer can legitimately change, which is exactly the invariant violation the tier exists to prevent.
table_self_checks._banned_substring_why: App Runner stopped accepting new customers in April 2026 and is banned repo-wide, including in trigger text. A candidate list is the likeliest place for it to creep back in.

deterministic_mappings._why: Each row below is a target that a plausible improviser gets WRONG, and the wrong answer is recorded in must_not_be so the failure message can name it.

azurerm_storage_account.assets.why: The account's blob surface maps to S3 with condition Always. Its account_kind is StorageV2, so the FileStorage exception does not apply. The presence of an SMB file share on this account must NOT drag the account itself to FSx — owner decision 11.5 disturbs no row, because the share is a separate resource.

azurerm_storage_share.reports.why: enabled_protocol is SMB, and protocol is the whole rubric (decision 11.5). EFS is the NFS branch and is the improviser's answer because EFS is the better-known file service. S3 would mean the share inherited its parent account's target, which children never do.

azurerm_cosmosdb_account.catalog.why: kind MongoDB / capability EnableMongo. DynamoDB is the improviser's answer because Cosmos-to-DynamoDB is the famous pairing, but it is only correct for the Core (SQL) API. The Mongo wire protocol makes DocumentDB a drop-in and DynamoDB a rewrite.

azurerm_eventhub_namespace.telemetry.why: kafka_enabled is true, and protocol is the whole rubric with no throughput threshold (decision 11.4). Kinesis is the improviser's answer because Event Hubs is usually described as Azure's Kinesis; it is correct only for native AMQP/SDK consumers, and it would be a code rewrite for a Kafka client.

confidence._why: A deterministic label claims the target came from a table row and no rubric ran. The asserter therefore checks BOTH directions: every expected row carries the label, and every entry carrying the label names a type that actually exists in direct_mappings. The second half is the one that catches an improvised label.

app_service_plan_fan_in._why: The single most expensive error in the whole skill. Five apps on one S1 plan cost one S1; five compute line items would be a 5x estimate error that Estimate cannot recover from, because by then the apps look like independent workloads.
app_service_plan_fan_in._expected_site_entry_count_why: Microsoft.Web/sites must produce ZERO entries in services[] and ZERO in pending_rubric[]. An app is a deployment onto its plan, not a compute unit.

unknown_type_stop._why: Owner decision: an UNTRANSLATED type is treated as cost-bearing by default and STOPs. It has no SKU, no consumption row, and no provider namespace, so the three-part cost-bearing test cannot clear it — and the skill cannot demonstrate that a resource it could not name is free. Warn-and-skip here would understate the estate with nothing to signal it.
unknown_type_stop._must_not_appear_why: The failure this pins is the SILENT one: recording the type as an ordinary skip satisfies every shape assertion, lets the phase emit HANDOFF_OK, and produces an estimate that is quietly missing a resource.

missing_rubric_halt._why: Same guard and same reasoning as discover-iac.md Step 2. 'No rubric is needed' and 'the rubric has not been written yet' are otherwise indistinguishable, and improvising past the second yields a mapping that satisfies every shape assertion and carries a confidence label it did not earn.

skips._why: A skipped resource must be RECORDED, never silently absent: a resource with no warnings[] entry is indistinguishable from one the design forgot. Conversely it must produce no services[] entry — an observability resource given a CloudWatch target would be a mapping claim there is no import path for.
skips._config_source_why: These two are read for their edges BEFORE being skipped, so their warning must say what they contributed. A bare 'skipped' loses the app-to-data edge's provenance, and that edge is what merges rg-app and rg-data during clustering.

hard_blocker._why: Azure Edition Windows Server is a statement, not a question: MGN refuses the image until it is re-imaged, so there is no option to weigh. A plausible improviser maps the VM to EC2 and says nothing, which is a migration that fails at replication time.

deferred_shape._why: A deferral did not come from a rubric, so labelling it `inferred` would claim reasoning that did not happen. The corpus fires no gate, so this check is vacuous today and exists to bind the shape before a gate fixture lands.

accounting._why: The catch-all. Every inventory resource must appear somewhere — mapped, pending, deferred, or explicitly skipped. Without this, dropping a resource is invisible: the design still parses, every other assertion still passes, and the estimate is simply missing a line.

forbidden_substrings._why: Banned repo-wide. Checked over the whole artifact, not just aws_service, because it creeps in through rationale prose and candidate lists.
